questions.question: What are the three primary colors?
questions.explanation: Red, yellow, and blue are the primary colors because you can't create them by mixing other colors together.
questions.funFact: Sir Isaac Newton invented the first color wheel in 1666!

questions.question: Which famous artist painted the 'Mona Lisa'?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa during the Italian Renaissance.
questions.funFact: The Mona Lisa is surprisingly small; it's only 30 inches tall and 21 inches wide!

questions.question: What do we call a painting of unmoving objects, like a bowl of fruit or flowers?
questions.explanation: A still life is a work of art depicting mostly inanimate subject matter.
questions.funFact: Ancient Egyptians painted still lifes in tombs because they believed the food depicted would become real in the afterlife!

questions.question: What type of instrument is a drum?
questions.explanation: Percussion instruments are played by hitting, shaking, or scraping them.
questions.funFact: The oldest known drum is the alligator drum, which was made in China from clay and alligator skin over 4,000 years ago!

questions.question: What do we call the written pages that actors read to learn their lines for a play?
questions.explanation: A script contains all the dialogue and stage directions for a play or movie.
questions.funFact: The word 'script' comes from the Latin word 'scriptus', which simply means 'written'!

questions.question: What is the art of beautiful, decorative handwriting called?
questions.explanation: Calligraphy uses special pens or brushes to make writing look like art.
questions.funFact: In ancient China, calligraphy was considered one of the highest forms of visual art!

questions.question: Which two colors do you mix together to make purple?
questions.explanation: Mixing the primary colors red and blue creates the secondary color purple.
questions.funFact: In ancient times, purple dye was so expensive to make from sea snails that only royalty was allowed to wear it!

questions.question: Which artist is famous for painting 'The Starry Night' and cutting off a piece of his own ear?
questions.explanation: Vincent van Gogh was a Dutch painter who created 'The Starry Night' while staying in an asylum.
questions.funFact: Van Gogh only ever sold one painting while he was alive, but today his works are worth millions!

questions.question: What is a group of people singing together called?
questions.explanation: A choir is a musical ensemble of singers.
questions.funFact: Singing in a choir has been scientifically proven to sync up the heartbeats of everyone singing!

questions.question: What kind of paint is transparent and mixed with water?
questions.explanation: Watercolor paints use water to thin the pigment, creating a light, see-through effect on paper.
questions.funFact: During the Renaissance, watercolors were mostly used just for quick sketches before the 'real' oil painting started!

questions.question: What is the wooden frame called that holds an artist's canvas while they paint?
questions.explanation: An easel stands upright to hold a canvas at eye level so the artist can paint comfortably.
questions.funFact: The word 'easel' comes from an old Dutch word meaning 'donkey', because it carries a heavy load!

questions.question: What do we call a painting of outdoor scenery, like mountains or the ocean?
questions.explanation: A landscape shows the natural environment, like forests, rivers, or mountains.
questions.funFact: Before the 1500s, landscapes were mostly just used as backgrounds for paintings of people!

questions.question: Which of these instruments has strings and is usually played with a bow?
questions.explanation: A violin is a string instrument, and the bow rubbed against the strings makes the sound.
questions.funFact: The hair on a violin bow is usually made from real horsehair!

questions.question: In a dance performance, what does a choreographer do?
questions.explanation: A choreographer invents and arranges the dance routines for the performers.
questions.funFact: Choreographers don't just work in dance; they also choreograph stage combat and sword fights in action movies!

questions.question: What type of theater uses puppets that are controlled from above using strings?
questions.explanation: Marionettes are puppets manipulated by strings attached to a control bar.
questions.funFact: Some complex marionettes can have over 30 strings to control individual fingers and facial expressions!

questions.question: What material is pottery usually made from before it is baked in an oven?
questions.explanation: Potters shape wet clay into bowls or vases, and then it hardens when baked.
questions.funFact: The special oven used to bake and harden pottery is called a kiln, and it can reach temperatures over 2000 degrees Fahrenheit!

questions.question: What do you call a picture made by arranging many small colored stones, tiles, or pieces of glass?
questions.explanation: A mosaic is created by piecing together tiny fragments to form a larger image.
questions.funFact: The ancient Romans decorated the floors of their homes with massive mosaics that worked like durable carpets!

questions.question: Colors that are opposite each other on the color wheel, like red and green, are called what?
questions.explanation: Complementary colors make each other look brighter when placed side by side.
questions.funFact: This is why sports teams often use complementary colors, like orange and blue, for their uniforms—it makes them stand out!

questions.question: What is it called when an artist makes a statue by chipping away stone with a chisel?
questions.explanation: Carving is a subtractive process where material is removed to create a shape.
questions.funFact: Michelangelo believed that the sculpture was already inside the stone, and he just had to carve away the extra pieces to set it free!

questions.question: In music, what is the steady beat that you can tap your foot to called?
questions.explanation: Rhythm is the pattern of sounds and silences in music that creates the beat.
questions.funFact: Your heartbeat will actually speed up or slow down to match the rhythm of the music you are listening to!
